selected_mechanism: Shared capacity visibility enables reversible anticipatory coordination. Regional teams identify partners and assemble a provisional plan before formal authorization, converting central approval from a search-and-initiation stage into a ratification stage.
explanatory_gain: The mechanism explains why added formal control coincided with faster response without claiming that approval itself caused speed. It locates the change in the sequencing and function of approval.

evidence_coverage.E1: Establishes the additional formal approval requirement.
evidence_coverage.E2: Shows faster resolution and increased lateral communication.
evidence_coverage.E3: Describes provisional reservation and plan assembly before approval.
evidence_coverage.E4: Shows that managers usually verified rather than originated solutions.

rival_accounts: Incident difficulty may have changed despite the available comparison.
Managers may have informally delegated authority independent of the dashboard.
observations_against: Managers frequently originate or materially revise proposed reallocations.
Lateral planning persists when capacity information is unavailable.
The same acceleration occurs for irreversible, high-liability actions.

prospective_transfer_predictions.claim: The mechanism should travel when capacity is mutually visible, provisional commitments are reversible, and the approver usually ratifies well-supported plans.
The mechanism should fail when decisions are irreversible or carry high liability, because authorization should remain the initiating stage.
The mechanism should weaken when dashboard information is stale or distrusted.

residual_anomalies: The current packet cannot isolate dashboard visibility from concurrent informal delegation.
